title: Interleaved length-aware slot weighting for continuous scheduler
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short user prompts followed by long generated responses, or vice versa) create suboptimal slot utilization and KV residency churn in the continuous scheduler. Current continuous batching treats slots fairly and queues by arrival time which causes: 1) long-response tasks to hold slots and KV residency for extended windows, increasing fragmentation and preventing short requests from getting low-latency service; 2) KV cache churn when long sequences evict hot prefixes for short-turn conversational workloads.

Goal: Implement an interleaved length-aware slot weighting mechanism in the continuous scheduler that dynamically assigns fractional slot weights and priority boost to short-turn tasks while guaranteeing throughput for long responses. The mechanism should reduce tail latency for short requests, lower KV eviction rate for hot prefixes, and avoid catastrophic GPU slab fragmentation. This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarking, and rollout gating for runtime-1.24.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler exposes a configurable slot_weight function that takes request_length_estimate and kv_residency_hint and returns a fractional weight (0.1 - 2.0)
End-to-end e2e latency P95 for short-turn requests (<=64 tokens) improves by >= 20% on representative mixed workload compared to baseline continuous scheduler
KV eviction rate for hot prefixes decreases by >= 15% under mixed traffic (measured by eviction/sec and miss ratio) without increasing long-response latency by more than 10%
No regression in end-to-end throughput beyond 5% on steady-state long-sequence benchmarks
Feature gated behind runtime-1.24 flag with A/B rollout and automatic rollback on degraded metrics
test_plan: Synthetic replay using production trace slice (2026-01-mixed-prompts) with 30% short-turn, 50% medium, 20% long responses; run 3x at 10k req/sec
Run per-GPU GPU-memory heatmap capture and KV-residency logs; compare fragmentation score before/after
Measure latency histogram (P50/P90/P95/P99) per length cohort and compute weighted SLA metric
Run canary in dedicated staging cluster region-eu with 5% traffic, monitor metrics for 24h, then extend to 25% if stable
Unit tests for slot_weight function and integration tests for scheduler's admission path
rollback_plan: Flip runtime-1.24.slot_weighting feature flag to OFF (instant) -> scheduler reverts to baseline weighting
If KV eviction or GPU fragmentation regresses above thresholds, rollback immediately and collect diagnostic bundle (kv_snapshot, slab_histograms) for postmortem
Hold traffic and route new sessions to fallback cluster running stable runtime-1.23 if automated rollback can't stabilize within 15 minutes
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with runtime and infra; sketched slot_weight API and data telemetry points (kv_residency_hint, estimated_output_tokens)
2026-02-22: Prototype slot_weight policy implemented in scheduler branch feature/length-weighting; basic unit tests passing
2026-03-01: Benchmarks on smallscale cluster: short-turn P95 improved ~18% but KV eviction unchanged -> adjusted weight curve to factor in kv_residency_hint
2026-03-07: Integrated GPU slab defragmentation hook to trigger soft compaction when fractional occupancy passes 85% during long-response spikes
2026-03-10: Canary config prepared for staging with 5% traffic; monitoring dashboards added for weighted-SLA and kv-eviction-rate
decision_log: Decision 2026-02-19: Use fractional slot weights (float) rather than hard slot preemption to minimize jitter and priority inversion in continuous batching

Decision 2026-02-25: Include kv_residency_hint supplied by tokenizer/service layer to bias weighting for requests that share prefixes; reasoning: reduces unnecessary eviction of hot prefixes without complex online profiling
Decision 2026-03-03: Implement conservative GPU compaction (soft compaction) triggered by slab heat thresholds rather than continuous compaction to avoid throughput cliffs
Trade-off: Aggressive weighting helps short requests but can increase tail for long responses; we will tune guardrails to cap long-response slowdown at 10%
